sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Redwood County, Minnesota?
sections.html:
Two offices in the Redwood County Government Center, 403 South Mill Street in Redwood Falls, split the work. The Assessor (507-637-4008) values and classifies every parcel, and the Auditor-Treasurer (507-637-4013) sends the bills and takes the payments. Jesse Jacobson is the County Assessor and Jean Price is the Auditor-Treasurer.

The Recorder, who files your deed after a sale, works from the same building at 507-637-4032. Mail for any of the three goes to P.O. Box 130, Redwood Falls, MN 56283. The assessor answers phones on weekdays from 8 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon.

sections.h2: What does Redwood County look like to a home seller?
sections.html:
Redwood County covers 882 square miles of rolling farmland in southwest Minnesota, with the Minnesota River along its northeastern edge and the Redwood and Cottonwood Rivers cutting east across it. Corn and soybeans dominate the land. Redwood Falls, the county seat and largest city, had 5,102 residents in 2020 and sits on U.S. Highway 71 with state highways 19 and 67 crossing town.

The county has fifteen cities: Belview, Clements, Delhi, Lamberton, Lucan, Milroy, Morgan, Redwood Falls, Revere, Sanborn, Seaforth, Vesta, Wabasso, Walnut Grove and Wanda. The Lower Sioux Indian Reservation lies entirely inside the county, in Paxton and Sherman townships. Alexander Ramsey Park, which the city took over from the state in 1958, is the best known public green space in Redwood Falls.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for Redwood County show a market where prices are modest and the population is slowly shrinking:

  • 15,265 residents in July 2025, down 1.0% from the April 2020 base, spread at about 17.6 people per square mile.
  • Homes that their owners live in carry a median value of $158,200 for 2020 to 2024, and 78.4% of homes are owner-occupied.
  • Median gross rent of $757, and 6,293 households.
  • Only 7 building permits issued in 2025, so most buyers choose from older houses.

With values in that range, a few hundred dollars of unpaid tax or a penalty can matter to a buyer's lender, so settle the balance before you list.

sections.h2: When are Redwood County property taxes due in 2026?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is paid in two halves, May 15 and October 15, and both 2026 dates have passed. The next deadline is tomorrow: agricultural land and manufactured homes owe their second half on Monday, November 16.

Redwood County 2026 property tax due dates, from the Auditor/Treasurer page
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estateFriday, May 15Thursday, October 15
Agricultural real estateFriday, May 15Monday, November 16
Personal propertyFriday, May 15None
Manufactured homeMonday, August 31Monday, November 16

Minnesota Statutes section 279.01 adds a 2% penalty on homestead and 4% on nonhomestead property once a due date is missed. The county charges a $30 fee on any returned check, failed electronic payment or reversed payment.

sections.h2: How can you pay property tax to the Redwood County Auditor-Treasurer?
sections.html:
The county runs an online payment page with a tax parcel lookup, and you can also pay at the Government Center or by mail. Owners who prefer not to remember dates can enroll in the Direct Payment Plan, which pulls money from a checking or savings account twice a year or once a year. Call 507-637-4013 to sign up or ask for the form.

If your lender pays through escrow, check the statement anyway. A seller who is closing soon should ask the Auditor-Treasurer for a current payoff figure for the parcel, since that office also posts the yearly delinquent tax list and the forfeited property sale notices.

sections.h2: How does the Redwood County assessor set your value?
sections.html:
The assessor's job is to give every parcel a use-based classification and an estimated market value as of January 2. Appraisers physically inspect each property at least once every five years under Minnesota Statutes section 273.01, and exempt property every six years. New construction and changes can trigger an extra visit.

Each spring the county mails a notice showing your value and class. That value drives the tax bill for the following year, so a mistake in square footage or condition carries forward.

  • Homestead status needs the owner to occupy the home as a primary residence, with an application filed by December 31 of the assessment year.
  • Owners who are blind or permanently disabled can apply for a special homestead class.
  • The disabled veterans' homestead exclusion form comes from the Assessor's office on request.
  • Special agricultural homestead forms are also available from that office.

sections.h2: What is the process for contesting a Redwood County valuation?
sections.html:
Start by calling the Assessor at 507-637-4008 and explaining what looks wrong. If you still disagree, appear before the local board of appeal and equalization for your city or township. The Assessor's office hosts these meetings in April, and in 2024 they ran from April 8 through April 24. Generally you must appear at the local board before the county board will hear you.

Under section 274.01 the local board meets between April 1 and May 31 and cannot lower the assessor's total by more than one percent. The Redwood County Board of Appeal and Equalization convened on June 16, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in the Commissioner's Room at the Government Center, where the commissioners heard one parcel and denied the requested change. A further route is a petition to district court or the Tax Court, which section 278.01 says must be filed by April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

sections.h2: What happens if Redwood County tax is unpaid when you sell?
sections.html:
On the first business day of January, any unpaid tax is deemed delinquent and an extra 2% is added under section 279.02. The county then publishes the delinquent parcel list. The Auditor-Treasurer's page also carries a forfeited property tax sale notice and a list of sales with surplus proceeds and unexpired claims.

A sale cannot finish cleanly until the tax is cleared. Under section 272.12 the county auditor must note that no delinquent taxes are owed before the Recorder will accept a deed, with exceptions such as probate deeds of distribution and transfer on death deeds. A title company normally pays the balance from the seller's proceeds, so ask for the payoff early.

sections.h2: What should a Redwood County seller do before closing?
sections.html:
A short list keeps the closing from stalling.

  • Pull your 2026 statement and confirm both halves show paid, or get the Auditor-Treasurer's payoff figure.
  • Read this spring's valuation notice and call the Assessor if the class or square footage is wrong.
  • Submit the electronic certificate of real estate value, which the Recorder's page says must be filed electronically for sales since October 1, 2014.
  • Tell the buyer about homestead. Under section 272.115 the assessor removes homestead classification from a sold property for the next assessment year unless the new owner applies and qualifies.
  • Ask the Recorder at 507-637-4032 about the deed recording fee and any search charges.

faqs.q: What is the next Redwood County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: Monday, November 16, 2026, for the second half on agricultural land and manufactured homes. Real estate second halves were due October 15. For regular real estate the next due date is the first half in May, and your statement lists the exact day.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute my Redwood County home value?
faqs.a: Call the County Assessor at 507-637-4008 on a weekday morning or afternoon until 4:30 If the call does not settle it, attend your city or township local board of appeal and equalization in April, then the county board in June.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Redwood County house that has unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, but the tax has to be cleared first. The auditor must certify that no delinquent tax is owed before a deed can be recorded, and the balance is usually paid from your sale proceeds. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-637-4013 for a payoff.

faqs.q: When must I apply for homestead in Redwood County?
faqs.a: By December 31 of the assessment year. The home must be owned and lived in by the owner, or by a qualified relative, as of January 2 or December 1. The Assessor's office handles every homestead application.

faqs.q: Does a buyer keep my homestead classification in Redwood County?
faqs.a: No. After a sale or transfer the assessor removes homestead status for the following assessment year unless the buyer files a homestead application and qualifies. Buyers should apply promptly after closing.
